attempted_claim: Let (X,O(1)) be a smoothable nodal quintic Calabi-Yau threefold in P^4 with exactly one ordinary double point x, with Hein-Sun unique weak Ricci-flat Kahler metric omega_0 in 2pi c_1(O(1)) polynomially asymptotic to the Stenzel cone at x and holomorphic volume form Omega_0 on X^{reg}. Does there exist a compact base B homeomorphic to S^3, a closed discriminant Delta in B with B\Delta dense open, and a continuous surjection f:X->B such that: (a) for every b in B\Delta the fibre F_b=f^{-1}(b) in X^{reg} is a smooth 3-torus calibrated by Re(e^{i theta(b)} Omega_0) for some phase theta(b); (b) for generic b in Delta the fibre F_b is a singular special Lagrangian integral current whose only singularities are Harvey-Lawson U(1)^2-invariant T^2-cone singularities and U(1)-invariant edge singularities of Joyce's local models, with Delta locally a codimension-one ribbon thickening of a trivalent graph separating two smooth special Lagrangian torus families limiting to the same conical fibre from opposite sides as currents; (c) near x, f is C^1-asymptotic to an explicit U(1)-invariant special Lagrangian fibration of the Stenzel cone; and (d) for a smoothing family X_t->X with glued Ricci-flat metrics, f is the flat limit as integral currents of special Lagrangian torus fibrations f_t:X_t->B?
decisive_failure: The lane attempted three concrete routes (global GMT minimizers, McLean plus Stenzel cone gluing, smoothing flat limits) plus a bounded U(1)-reduction computation on the Stenzel cone. All terminate at established open problems: compact calibrated SYZ existence, 3-d special Lagrangian uniqueness and classification, Joyce stable-singularity and ribbon-discriminant conjectures, and phase stability through nodal collapse. No partial theorem or independently valuable finding was proved.
